claim.quote: The achieved level of radiopurity of NaI(Tl) crystals makes construction of a dark matter detector possible.

key_value_text.quote: The concentration of natural potassium in NaI(Tl) crystal was reduced down to 20 ppb.
key_value_text.value: The concentration of natural potassium in NaI(Tl) crystal was reduced down to 20 ppb.

name: Development of highly radiopure NaI(Tl) scintillator for PICOLON dark matter search project

published.quote: Progress of Theoretical and Experimental Physics, Volume 2021, Issue 4, April 2021, 043F01

summary.plain: The PICOLON group reduced the radioactive impurities in its sodium iodide crystals enough to build a dark matter detector: natural potassium down to 20 ppb and no significant lead-210 excess.
summary.technical: Hybrid purification: recrystallisation reduces 40K (natural K down to 20 ppb) and resins reduce the U and Th chains: thorium series 1.2 +- 1.4 uBq/kg, 226Ra 13 +- 4 uBq/kg, 210Pb below 5.7 uBq/kg at 90% C.L. (Prog. Theor. Exp. Phys. 2021, 043F01).

title: Development of highly radiopure NaI(Tl) scintillator for PICOLON dark matter search project
why_it_matters: It is the crystal development on which the PICOLON measurements rest.
